newsitem.title: UK: MARK STEADY ON CROSSES, EYES DOLLAR/MARK DIP.
newsitem.headline: MARK STEADY ON CROSSES, EYES DOLLAR/MARK DIP.

text.p: The mark was mostly steady on its crosses in Europe and underpinned as the spectre of EMU delay resurfaced alongside nerves about German rates, said traders.
A slide in dollar/mark, which shed near a pfennig from early highs, also helped the mark on its Euro crosses, said traders.
"The main theme in continental Europe is German rate fears...That should give the deutschmark some support," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
But the mark was off peaks scaled on Wednesday after the Bundesbank warned the pace of inflation had picked up and fresh talk of a delay to European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Talk of EMU delay resurfaced on Wednesday after a commentary in Britain's Evening Standard newspaper -- dismissed as "pure speculation" by Bonn -- said Germany and France might delay EMU for a year if Britain agreed to join the starting line.
Traders said the story, however, was still affecting markets on Thursday as it pushed sterling/mark and dollar/mark lower.
"Maybe it's speculation, but sterling/mark is being sold off on the back of it," said a currency trader.
At 0915 GMT, mark/French franc was at 3.3709/14 against 3.3719/24 in late Europe on Wednesday. Mark/Spanish peseta stood at 84.51/53 against 84.54/59.
The mark, however, was well off peaks of 84.62 pesetas -- a three-month high -- hit Wednesday. Mark/Italian lira stood at 978.20/8.50 against 978.50/978.70 in late Europe.
"Any talk of EMU delay helps the mark...The EMU-delay story has really been hitting the high-yielders," said Stamenkovic.
With countries such as Italy and Spain racing to streamline their economies to ensure a place at EMU's start-line, a delay could prompt an easing of fiscal targets.
"If EMU were delayed, the pressure for them to continue to follow these policies may not be as strong as it was," Stamenkovic added. He said a delay, however, was unlikely.
